question: A 59-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-year history of nausea and chronic abdominal pain that is worse after eating. She has Hashimoto thyroiditis. She does not smoke or drink alcohol. A biopsy specimen of the corpus of the stomach shows destruction of the upper glandular layer of the gastric mucosa and G-cell hyperplasia. This patient is at greatest risk for which of the following conditions?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Hashimoto thyroiditis -> chronic abdominal pain -> destruction of upper glandular layer of gastric mucosa -> G-cell hyperplasia -> increased risk of gastric adenocarcinoma -> 80%
CHAIN: Hashimoto thyroiditis -> chronic abdominal pain -> destruction of upper glandular layer of gastric mucosa -> G-cell hyperplasia -> increased risk of gastric MALT lymphoma -> 75%
analysis: The patient's presentation with chronic abdominal pain, nausea, destruction of the upper glandular layer of the gastric mucosa, and G-cell hyperplasia suggests a diagnosis of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. This syndrome is characterized by gastrin-secreting tumors (gastrinomas) that lead to gastric acid hypersecretion, causing peptic ulcers and potentially increasing the risk of gastric adenocarcinoma.
